open_obligations: Check whether evaluation-easier holds on hard MATH levels for the specific Llemma models.
Note Leike et al.'s caveat that the assumption fails for low-dimensional outcomes unless explanations are evaluated.
Check whether process reward models evaluate explanations in Leike et al.'s sense.
out.other_title: Assumption 2: evaluating outcomes is easier than producing correct behavior
out.rationale: Leike et al.'s Assumption 2 is that for many tasks evaluating outcomes is easier than producing correct behaviour. Sun et al. state their method is motivated by evaluation being easier than generation and train a verifier on easy tasks to supervise a generator on hard tasks; their finding that evaluators generalise easy-to-hard better than generators is consistent with but does not prove the assumption.
out.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: using evaluators to supervise generators beyond the supervisor's reach, premised on evaluation being easier than generation

open_obligations: Check that Sun et al.'s PRM800K subset is restricted to levels 1-3.
Note that Sun et al. also introduce an outcome-and-process reward model (OPRM).
out.rationale: Lightman et al. define ORMs trained on final results and PRMs trained on per-step feedback. Sun et al. train ORMs and PRMs only on labelled easy MATH problems (levels 1-3, including PRM800K data) and use them as evaluators to supervise generators on hard problems by re-ranking or RL.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: outcome- and process-supervised reward models used to supervise generators, extended to training only on easy problems

text: Motivated by the observation that evaluation is easier than generation, the authors hypothesize that an evaluator can offer easy-to-hard generalization useful for improving a generator: first train a verifier on easy tasks, then use its generalization to supervise the generator on hard tasks. They train outcome-supervised and process-supervised reward models as easy-to-hard evaluators on labeled easy tasks paired with unlabeled hard tasks given only as questions.
title: Train a verifier on easy tasks, then use it to supervise the generator on hard tasks
